reason: The cited evidence supports the capability of the melt printing method to rapidly melt and uniformly mix multi-element powders into homogeneous alloys at up to 3000 K, but it does not mention W-Cu systems, post-processing heat treatment, or any comparison with spark plasma sintering, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Ultrahigh-temperature melt printing can achieve rapid melting and uniform mixing of multi-element powders up to 3000 K
The method can produce homogeneous alloys with uniform grain size
Post-processing heat treatment can further improve microstructure and properties of the printed alloy

The resulting W-Cu alloy will outperform spark plasma sintering in thermal transport and mechanical durability
